fix(prometheus): preserve persistent storage

# What does this PR do?

Preserves managed Prometheus PVCs when Prometheus is disabled, its configuration or storage is removed, or the monitoring release is uninstalled. Stored metrics are deleted only through an explicit manual PVC deletion.

The change removes the legacy fixed-name PVC deletion, adds reconciliation coverage for retention scenarios, and updates uninstall and Prometheus-to-VictoriaMetrics migration documentation.

## Why

The current reconciler deletes `prometheus-k8s-db-prometheus-k8s-0` before checking the component state. A configuration change made during the managed Prometheus deprecation window can therefore remove stored metrics without a separate destructive decision.

Closes #505.

Follow-up findings from the Kind check are tracked separately in #507 and #508.

## Verification

- `make test`
- Controller regression coverage for missing configuration, `install=false`, removed storage, pause, and repeated reconciliation
- Kind lifecycle check: persistent Prometheus became available, ordinary Helm uninstall removed PlatformMonitoring, the Prometheus CR, StatefulSet, and pod, while the same PVC and PV remained Bound
- Independent review completed with no remaining findings

## Checklist

- [x] `make generate` is not required because the public API did not change
- [x] `make test` passes
- [x] User-facing uninstall and migration documentation is updated

fix(cli): add --pre-remove to project set-config

Code changes: +8 -3
Tests: +53 -1
Others: +6 -0

## What

`ao project set-config` can now set Cleanup (`preRemove`) scripts with a flag:

- A new repeatable `--pre-remove` flag (mirroring `--post-create`) sets Cleanup scripts via field flags, e.g. `ao project set-config <id> --pre-remove "docker compose down -v"`.
- `pre-remove` joins `projectConfigFlags`, so the flag edits only `preRemove` in the saved config and leaves the rest of it intact.
- The `using-ao` skill's `project` page documents the flag and adds an example.

## Why

Covers the remaining part of #7514 now that #7318 has merged:

- #7318 is on `main`: the CLI's `projectConfig` mirror models `PreRemove`, and set-config flags use read-modify-write, so `--config-json` carries `"preRemove": [...]` through to `PUT /api/v1/projects/{id}/config` instead of dropping it.
- What was still missing was any way to set Cleanup scripts from the CLI at all: there was no flag for them.
- This PR adds the flag and wires it into the same read-modify-write path. Rebased onto current `main` so it no longer duplicates #7318.

## Testing

- `TestProjectSetConfig_PreRemoveFlags`: two `--pre-remove` values reach the PUT body in order.
- `TestProjectSetConfig_PreRemoveConfigJSON`: `--config-json` with `postCreate` and `preRemove` sends both.
- `TestCanonicalConfigPreservesExistingSettings` stores a `preRemove` entry and asserts it survives the get → write-back round-trip.
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./internal/cli/...`, `gofmt` clean.
- `go test ./internal/cli/ ./internal/skillassets/`: pass except the pre-existing Windows symlink failure in `TestRenderCheckReplacesItsEarlierScreenshot`, which reproduces on unpatched `main` on this machine; pinned Linux CI is the arbiter.

## Intentional omissions

- No `--pre-remove` on `ao project add`; `add` builds only agent-override config today and this stays out of scope.

fix(review): show the saved reason when a manual review fails

Code changes: +16 -14\
Tests: +21 -0\
Others: +0 -0

## What

Show a failed manual review's saved reason in Review controls, including when Auto review is off.

## Why

Fixes #6107. The daemon already returns the failed run's body. Main's renderer only shows failure bodies for auto-triggered reviews, leaving manual failures without that reason.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Main `9041e10a6c1dd0acb3e254063265d03ee95268d1`: Reviews omits the saved reason for a failed manual run. | Head `205aa9b00e1c07779c2bf45b4c379e036c0299e9`: Review controls shows "Review Failed" and the saved reason with Auto review off. |

Images to attach: before `6107-main-9041e10-hidden-reason.png`; after `6107-head-205aa9b-reason-shown.png`. Real macOS Electron captures with isolated seeded review records and Auto review off.

## How

Include failed manual runs when choosing the latest failure notice. Keep the Auto review preference gate for auto-triggered failures and the existing 10-second dismissal. Label a manual failure "Review Failed".

Related #7169 handles reviewer errors in the CLI. This fixes display of the persisted reason in the desktop app. It leaves the trigger endpoint's generic error envelope unchanged.

## Testing

- Focused inspector file: 171 tests passed.
- `npm run typecheck` in `frontend/`: passed.
- Real Electron before/after with identical failed/manual/body facts returned by the daemon. The notice appeared on the head and later dismissed. Both saved captures inspected.
- Local ACP peer with no live model call. I seeded the existing failed-run record; I did not create a new reviewer failure or test the trigger toast.
- Full suites and platform jobs left to remote CI.

AO native review approved the pinned head with no required changes. All current remote CI checks passed.

## Checklist

- [x] Branched from current `origin/main`
- [x] One focused change; links #6107
- [x] Follows AGENTS.md conventions
- [ ] Before / After images attached (captures ready; upload held)
- [x] Regression test added for a failed manual review
- [x] Relevant CI checks pass (all current remote checks passed)

fix(teamcity): don't cut on escaped characters

As characters can be escaped with `|`, the cut should take care to not break an escaped sequence.

For example:

`golangci-lint|n` (length is `15`) with a limit of `14`, a raw cut will produce `golangci-lint|`.
But the last `|` is the escape character, so it cannot be alone.
The new implementation will reduce the limit to `13` instead of `14` to not break the escaped sequence, and will produce `golangci-lint`.

+++ b/pkg/printers/teamcity.go
@@ -126,9 +126,23 @@ func (i InspectionInstance) Print(w io.Writer, replacer *strings.Replacer) (int,
 }
 
 func cutVal(s string, limit int) string {
+	if limit <= 0 {
+		return ""
+	}
+
 	runes := []rune(s)
-	if len(runes) > limit {
-		return string(runes[:limit])
+	if len(runes) <= limit {
+		return s
+	}
+
+	var count int
+	for i := limit - 1; i >= 0 && runes[i] == '|'; i-- {
+		count++
 	}
-	return s
+
+	if count%2 == 1 {
+		limit--
+	}
+
+	return string(runes[:limit])
 }
